newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BT/MCI merge as EU opens its telecoms markets.
newsitem.headline: BT/MCI merge as EU opens its telecoms markets.

text.p: The planned merger between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp takes place against the backdrop of a major effort to open up the European Union's telecommunications markets to competition.
The EU has pledged to abolish all state monopolies over telecoms services and infrastructure in most countries by January 1, 1998.
That deadline will force governments to take the final liberalistion step by opening their lucrative voice telephone markets to competition.

The European Commission, arguing that a competitive telecoms market is essential for Europe's industrial competitiveness, has already used special treaty powers to issue a series of laws to pry open other sectors.

The EU executive ordered governments to introduce full competition in their mobile phone markets last January. Last year, it ordered them to allow cable TV networks by January 1, 1996 to carry telecoms services such as data transmission that had already been opened to competition.

The Commission also said earlier this year that governments must allow new telecoms operators to bypass state phone companies and use "alternative networks" such as those operated by utility companies to carry liberalised telecoms services by July 1, 1996.

It insisted that Germany and France issue licences to comply with that directive to win clearance of the Global One telecoms alliance between France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp of the United States.
Britain's telecoms market is already more open than those of most EU countries, with Mercury Communications, a unit of Cable and Wireless Plc, competing with BT to offer voice phone service.
The Commission has said that a key reason it cleared an earlier joint venture betweeh BT and MCI was that both the British and U.S. telecoms markets were relatively open to competition.
The EU rules allow Greece, Ireland, Portugal and Spain to request delays in implementing some of the telecoms liberalisation deadlines.
